rule: Excessive or premeditated celebrations banned (the 'Gastineau rule' after Mark Gastineau's sack dance); 15 yards
Lambeau Leap begins (LeRoy Butler, Dec 26 1993); later grandfathered as allowed
Tightened: choreographed group celebrations banned; Lambeau Leap grandfathered

Owners vote 29-3: 15 yards on the next kickoff for excessive celebration; leaving feet, going to the ground, or using props (incl. the ball, towels, phones) flagged; spikes, spins, dances still allowed
Goalpost/crossbar treated as a prop: dunking over the goalpost banned (Jimmy Graham, Calvin Johnson)

Loosened: going to the ground, using the ball as a prop, and group celebrations allowed; still flagged: goalpost as a prop, violent/sexual gestures, prolonged celebration delaying the game, outside props
Dead-ball unsportsmanlike foul after a TD can be enforced on the try or the kickoff
Taunting made a point of emphasis (two flags = ejection already standard); taunting flags spike that season
Excessive celebration and taunting are dead-ball unsportsmanlike fouls: 15 yards on the try or kickoff
Point of emphasis on excessive or prolonged celebrations; drawing attention to self banned
Live-ball unsportsmanlike conduct: taunting before crossing the goal line is enforced 15 yards from the spot of the foul and the touchdown comes off
High school (NFHS): unsportsmanlike conduct 15 yards; two unsportsmanlike fouls = disqualification; live-ball taunting before the goal line also cancels the score (enforced as a live-ball foul)
